newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Part of Saudi term mid-distillate sales concluded.
newsitem.headline: Part of Saudi term mid-distillate sales concluded.

text.p: State-owned Saudi Aramco has concluded diesel and jet-kerosene fuel term contracts for liftings in 1997 with at least two buyers, industry sources said on Tuesday.

They said the annual term tender to sell 0.5-percent sulphur diesel was awarded at between 90-cents and $1.00-per-barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, up from 1996 price of about 70 cents premium.

The 1.0-percent sulphur diesel was sold at about 65 cents premium to MidEast spot quotes fob. The jet-kerosene fuel was awarded at about 80 cents discount to Singapore spot quotes, fob basis, which is currently equivalent to around 60 cents over MidEast spot quotes fob.
Traders said Shell and Kuwait-based International Petroleum Group (IPG) were among the winners.
But sources in the two companies declined to comment, citing a confidentiality clause in the contract document.
Traders said more awards are likely later in the week to other traders as the contract is valid until October 31. But the price is not expected to vary substantially.
Among the players who are holders of term contracts currently include Thailand's International Oil Trading (IOT) and Singapore's Hin Leong Trading, traders said.
They said there was no confirmation whether or not talks between state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) and Aramco for up to 1.0 million tonnes of diesel have been finalised.
Aramco availabilities for the 1997 term contracts are less than 1996 due to increased domestic consumption and scheduled plant maintenance.
One source familiar with the talks said that a lot of the barrels offered were for lifting in the first half of 1997.
During the third quarter, the 325,000-barrel-per-day Rabigh refinery is due for maintenance turnaround, one trader said.
They added that Aramco prefers to keep its fourth quarter product for spot sales.
